question: At approximately the same routed-layer payload as route12/Budget16 IQ1_S, does broader STQ1_0 coverage reduce captured-state routed-output error enough to earn a terminal-KL experiment?

frozen_inputs.row_selection: first four validation rows in capture order
frozen_inputs.selector: abs(router_weight) times 10K mean omitted-slab residual norm, stable route then within-expert rank ties

format.stq1_0: format-equivalent PTQ emulation: {-d,0,+d}, stride-16 3:4 groups, fp16 scale per 256 weights, 42 bytes per block, three LS/selection iterations, no imatrix term
format.important_limitation: The local screen emulates decoded STQ values from the authoritative IQ1_S source. It does not perform physical STQ reads, run an STQ HIP kernel, or measure terminal logits.

metrics: routed-output cosine versus captured native route12 aggregate
exact source and used response artifact hashes

gate.go_to_terminal: At least one STQ arm has finite outputs and mean routed-output relative L2 no worse than route12_iq1s_b16 while staying within 1% of its declared bytes.
gate.retain_as_low_priority: The best STQ arm is worse than B16 but no more than 1.5x its mean relative L2; retain only for a terminally ranked exact-core plus STQ-tail test.
gate.no_go: Both STQ arms exceed 1.5x B16 mean relative L2, produce a non-finite value, or fail the format self-check.

scope: This is a cheap local discriminator only. Local error is known to be a weak terminal-value proxy, so even a GO cannot establish terminal KL, behavior, bytes/token, physical reads, or throughput. A HIP decoder remains unearned.
